about: What React Native's AccessibilityInfo tells an application of the session as it runs (sample/AccessibilityInfoProbe.tsx), through the real screen reader process (docs/adr/0014-screen-reader.mdx, decision 8) and the session's Reduce Transparency (docs/adr/0019-settings.mdx). The reader runs from the start: isScreenReaderEnabled() and isAccessibilityServiceEnabled() answer true at once, as the session told the window at connect, and no change is told. Super+F5 stops it: screenReaderChanged and accessibilityServiceChanged each fire once, false, and isScreenReaderEnabled() answers false then; Super+F5 starts it again, once more each, true. Toggle (granted `settings`, as the session grants Settings) turns Reduce Transparency on and off: isReduceTransparencyEnabled() answers it and reduceTransparencyChanged fires once each time, which React Native's Android AccessibilityInfo never did. Each step checks what React received (nothing but Toggle's press) and what was said. With the host answering that no assistive technology runs, the start shows false and no change is ever told, and it fails.
